lesson: [lfm2.5_1.2b_inst] Sweeping whole GQA groups (the 4 query heads sharing one KV head) was the most productive first pass. 37 of the 48 groups took about 2 seconds each. It surfaced L5 KV6 (heads 24-27: weekday .619, passed) and L14 KV2 (heads 8-11: month .255, passed); L14 head 8 has the model's largest out_proj norm, 7.6.

[lfm2.5_1.2b_inst] Canceller heads turn entangled heads into selective units. Ablating L10 heads 20-23 alone lowered loss on roman (-.26) and the calendar skills. Adding them to math heads 25/27 gave math .182 with every other skill ≤.05, confirmed on GSM8K (.80→.60). Adding heads 5-7 as well gave math .192 (GSM8K .80→.55). L12 head 11 (math .145 alone) plus KV group 6 gave math .181 (GSM8K .80→.50).

[lfm2.5_1.2b_inst] Map single heads before building sets. L10 head 9 alone dropped multilingual by .631; the screened 8-head set (8, 9, 20-23, 30, 31: .697) is head 9 plus passengers. At 12 heads, random same-size parts include head 9 and drop multilingual up to .79, so the screen fails. Keep a strong single-head core at ≤8 heads.

[lfm2.5_1.2b_inst] MLP clusters picked from weights were not causal in this model. 64-1024 units chosen by unembedding cosine (top unit .53-.60), by reading the screened heads' write subspace (.69 vs .48 mean) or by early-layer accented-token selectivity moved targets by under .1, and the L14 1024-unit set hurt every skill. Gate-row families (L10 unit 3890 has 19 near-duplicate w1 rows; its gate reads Cyrillic, Portuguese and CJK tokens) did drop multilingual by .35 at 64 units. But that effect needs the hub units 3890 and 947 together with the rest of the family: ranks 2-65 alone gave .008, and the full family also hit month by .58.

[lfm2.5_1.2b_inst] Out_proj subspace overlap with a known head predicted analogues in other layers. L5 KV group 2 overlapped L10 head 9's write space (.075-.08 vs .031 random; V overlap .154) and did carry multilingual (.15-.29). But roman, object_color or feminine side effects always exceeded target/3, so it never passed.

[lfm2.5_1.2b_inst] Narrow low-base skills (roman_numeral .08, month_successor .045) are noisy relative-drop metrics. Random same-size parts dropped them by up to .6, which failed L12 heads 16-19 (roman .398 vs random .437) and the 8-head L14 month set (.257 vs .265). Facts heads were always tied to roman (L10 h10: facts .172, roman .396). The cleanest facts set (L12 heads 4-6, 20, 24-27: .16) failed the held-out check; aim for a search drop above .25 before screening.

[lfm2.5_1.2b_inst] Seeded weight-similarity MLP families gave 46 passing parts of 64-512 units. Recipe: take 1-6 attribution seeds in one layer, score every unit by 0.5*cos(w2 column, mean seed column) + 0.5*cos(w1 row, mean seed row), subtract the max score against other skills' seeds and hubs, take the top K. Passes included L13 roman 512 (.978), L13 weekday 512 (.927), L13 color 512 (.762), L15 masculine 512 (.59) and L11 roman 512 (.753). Drops stayed flat from 64 to 512 units, so the seed carries the effect and the similarity filler mostly adds size.

[lfm2.5_1.2b_inst] Subtract hubs and neighbouring-skill seeds explicitly. Removing color/roman hub unit 2955 cut the L13 roman-128 color leak from .34 to under .1 (roman .967). Subtracting weekday_list_next units 2401/2678 from the L13 weekday family cut the list leak from .45 to .17 while keeping weekday at .93. Calendar hubs to remove: L10 3890, L9 6161, L6 4810, L7 1286, L8 3869.

[lfm2.5_1.2b_inst] Broad skills did not localize in MLP families. Code families at L5/L9/L10/L15 (64-256 units) dropped code at most .067. The L10 multilingual family dropped it .008 and the L15 math family .05. L15 facts families dropped facts .18-.19 but leaked general_text .09, over the limit. Don't spend screens on broad-skill MLP sets on this model.

[lfm2.5_1.2b_inst] Reading out_proj head slices through the unembedding found real-looking writers that weren't selective. L14 head 19 writes number words and ordinals across languages (11.9x random energy). L14 head 22 writes geographic entities (country names 6x, cities 5.5x), and L12 heads 16-20 do the same more weakly. Their quads gave only roman .155 (general_text .11) and facts .04-.13. L10 heads 8-11 dropped multilingual .765 but facts .26; L12 heads 8-11 dropped math .30 but calendar controls about .6.

[general] The screen checks only the target's own control, not other skills' controls. Pronoun families passed even though the opposite pronoun's control moved .4-.7 (e.g. L15 masculine 64: .622, own control .062, feminine control .687). Py handles are lowercased, so save /work files under lowercase names. The agent-skill cap is 8, so define broad, high-base skills before building narrow ones.
